penicillin.mechanism: Type I IgE-mediated immediate hypersensitivity or Type IV T-cell-mediated delayed immune reaction against the core beta-lactam thiazolidine ring structure.
penicillin.source: American Academy of Allergy, Asthma & Immunology (AAAAI)

explanations.simple: Potential allergy-related medication risk detected. You have reported a Penicillin allergy, and this medicine contains a penicillin-family compound that could cause severe hives, facial swelling, or anaphylaxis.
explanations.detailed: Penicillins share a common beta-lactam core. In allergic individuals, major determinant penicilloyl epitopes bind preformed IgE on mast cells and basophils, triggering degranulation and systemic anaphylaxis.
explanations.clinician: Contraindicated. Cross-reactivity among aminopenicillins (amoxicillin, ampicillin) is nearly 100%. Substitute with macrolides (Azithromycin) or fluoroquinolones (Ciprofloxacin) based on culture and susceptibility.

penicillin.precaution: Avoid use and consult a healthcare professional. Do not take this medication if you have a known penicillin allergy. Seek immediate emergency care for swelling of lips, throat, or difficulty breathing.

aspirin.mechanism: Potential allergy-related medication risk detected. Cyclooxygenase-1 inhibition shunts arachidonic acid metabolism to the 5-lipoxygenase pathway, leading to massive cysteinyl leukotriene overproduction (AERD).
aspirin.source: Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology & AAAAI

explanations.simple: Potential allergy-related medication risk detected. You reported an Aspirin/NSAID allergy. Taking this medication can trigger severe bronchospasms, severe facial hives, or respiratory distress.
explanations.detailed: Aspirin-Exacerbated Respiratory Disease (AERD) / NSAID hypersensitivity: COX-1 inhibition depletes prostaglandin E2 (a natural bronchodilator), removing the brake on 5-lipoxygenase and producing leukotrienes C4, D4, and E4.
explanations.clinician: Avoid use and consult a healthcare professional. Cross-reactivity between Aspirin and other non-selective COX-1 inhibitors (Ibuprofen, Diclofenac) approaches 90%. Use Paracetamol for analgesia, which is tolerated by >90% of AERD patients at doses <= 1000mg.

aspirin.precaution: Avoid use and consult a healthcare professional. Do not take Aspirin, Ibuprofen, or Diclofenac. Use Paracetamol for fever and pain instead.

nsaid.mechanism: Leukotriene overproduction or IgE-mediated anaphylaxis triggered by non-steroidal anti-inflammatory agents.

explanations.simple: Potential allergy-related medication risk detected. You are allergic to NSAIDs. This medication is an NSAID and may cause severe allergic reactions.
explanations.detailed: Patients with NSAID hypersensitivity cross-react with other agents in the same class due to shared COX-1 inhibition or common hapten structures.
explanations.clinician: Contraindicated. Switch to paracetamol or acetaminophen.

nsaid.precaution: Avoid use and consult a healthcare professional. Switch to Paracetamol.

sulfa.mechanism: Immune recognition of the arylsulfonamide or non-arylsulfonamide moiety causing cutaneous eruptions and allergic reactions.

explanations.simple: You reported a Sulfa allergy. This medication contains a sulfonamide chemical group that could trigger skin rashes or allergic swelling in sensitive individuals.
explanations.detailed: While cross-reactivity between antibiotic sulfonamides (arylamines) and non-antibiotic sulfonamides (diuretics, sulfonylureas) is clinically low (<10%), idiosyncratic hypersensitivity can still occur.
explanations.clinician: Use with caution. Non-arylamine sulfonamides lack the N4 aromatic amine essential for antibiotic sulfa IgE-mediated anaphylaxis, but patients with multiple drug allergies remain predisposed.

sulfa.precaution: Inform your physician of your sulfa allergy before starting this medication. Report any new rashes, hives, or itching immediately.

cephalosporin.mechanism: Immune hypersensitivity to the 7-aminocephalosporanic acid beta-lactam core or R1 side chains.

explanations.simple: You reported a Cephalosporin allergy. This medication is a cephalosporin antibiotic and could trigger severe allergic reactions.
explanations.detailed: Cephalosporin allergy involves antibodies directed against the bicyclic dihydrothiazine beta-lactam nucleus or specific R1/R2 side chains.
explanations.clinician: Avoid in patients with documented cephalosporin anaphylaxis. Substitute with azithromycin or ciprofloxacin based on clinical susceptibility.

cephalosporin.precaution: Do not take Cefixime. Consult your doctor for an alternative antibiotic family.

opioid.mechanism: Pseudoallergic non-immunologic mast cell degranulation or true IgE-mediated opioid hypersensitivity.

explanations.simple: You reported an opioid allergy or sensitivity. Tramadol works through opioid pathways and may cause flushing, hives, or severe reactions.
explanations.detailed: Opioids can directly stimulate mast cell MRGPRX2 receptors causing non-IgE histamine release, or rarely true IgE anaphylaxis.
explanations.clinician: Exercise caution. Evaluate if prior reaction was pseudoallergy (itching/flushing) or true anaphylaxis. Prefer non-opioid multimodal analgesia.

opioid.precaution: Avoid Tramadol. Use Paracetamol or safe non-opioid pain relievers.

statin.mechanism: Statin-associated muscle toxicity, immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy (anti-HMGCR antibodies), or hypersensitivity rash.

explanations.simple: You reported a statin intolerance or allergy. This cholesterol-lowering medication belongs to the statin family.
explanations.detailed: Statin intolerance involves severe myalgia, myopathy, or rare autoimmune anti-HMGCR myopathy. Cross-reactivity between lipophilic (atorvastatin) and hydrophilic (rosuvastatin) statins is variable.
explanations.clinician: Evaluate symptoms. If mild myalgia, consider low-dose alternate-day rosuvastatin or non-statin lipid lowering therapies (ezetimibe, PCSK9 inhibitors).

statin.precaution: Discuss alternative cholesterol medications with your cardiologist.

ciprofloxacin.mechanism: IgE-mediated hypersensitivity or MRGPRX2 receptor-mediated direct mast cell activation.
ciprofloxacin.source: Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology

explanations.simple: You reported an allergy to Ciprofloxacin or fluoroquinolones. Taking this can cause serious allergic reactions.
explanations.detailed: Fluoroquinolones exhibit class-wide cross-reactivity for both IgE-mediated anaphylaxis and direct mast cell degranulation.
explanations.clinician: Contraindicated. Avoid all fluoroquinolones. Select alternative antimicrobial class.

ciprofloxacin.precaution: Do not take Ciprofloxacin. Consult your doctor for an alternate antibiotic.
